Hi Maya — Marcus on infra here. Per Vanessa's ask, below is our recommended technical baseline and SKU mix for the 1.2B token/month baseline with 3x burst. I'll keep numbers conservative (sustained rates) and note trade-offs for latency vs cost.

Assumptions:
- Large model profile: gpt-4o-like, average seq 1k, 70% of traffic
- Mid-size profile: 13B open model, avg seq 512, 25% of traffic
- Embeddings/rerank: small models, N/A for GPU compute (serving on CPU/accelerators)

Sustained tokens/sec (sustained inference, single model warm):
- H100-80GB (fp8/quantized): ~11k tokens/sec for 1k-seq gpt-4o-like (sustained, single-concurrent-stream)
- A100-40GB (fp16): ~5.5k tokens/sec for same workload
- A10G / L4-class (quantized INT8 for smaller models): ~1.2–2k tokens/sec for 13B workloads

Recommended reserved pool (initial phase, target: handle baseline w/ headroom + 3x burst):
- 12 x H100 (primary, latency-sensitive traffic)
- 6 x A100 (mid-tier, cost-effective for steady-state batching)
- 8 x L4-class nodes (embeddings and smaller models)

Rationale: H100s provide best tail-latency and highest throughput for large sequences; A100s reduce cost for batched steady-state throughput. L4 nodes keep embedding costs low and reduce cross-queue contention on large GPUs.

Estimated coverage (sustained baseline):
- H100s cover ~0.85 of peak low-latency requests when concurrency constrained; A100s absorb high-batch workloads and background processing. Expected 99.95% availability with this mix given standard redundancy and our fallback model variants.

Notes on tail-latency and KV caching:
- We recommend prefix/KV caching for predictable prompt prefixes (e.g., system messages + common context) — this reduces per-token compute by ~15–25% for long seqs.
- Continuous batching windows tuned to 50–75ms in production deliver better unit cost with minimal tail impact for your workload profile.

I'll prepare a quick workbook showing tokens/sec vs concurrency per GPU and include a suggested phasing (trial -> 50% reserved -> 100% reserved).

— Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Hi John / Maya — appreciate the clear asks. Below is our concession tracker and proposed next steps; we can put these into a redline of procurement_terms_acme.docx after you confirm which options you prefer.

Concession tracker (options):
- Commitment tiers: 1) 1.2B tokens/mo baseline (no discount), 2) >=1.8B tokens/mo -> 12% discount, 3) >=3.0B tokens/mo -> 18% discount
- Ramp credit: one-time 10% usage credit applied across months 1–3 if you sign within 30 days of proposal
- Early-termination: limited protection — pro-rated credit for months 4–6 if utilization < 60% of committed baseline (credit equal to 50% of unused committed spend for months 4–6 only)
- SLA: Redwood will commit to 99.95% availability for Dedicated pools. SLA credit schedule: 10% of monthly committed fee for <99.95% and >=99.5%; 25% for <99.5%. (Full SLA in contract appendix)
- Audit/access: we provide KMS/HSM integration details and monthly access logs; full SOC2 package available under NDA.

Phasing proposal (we suggest):
1) Pilot (30 days): 4 x H100 + 2 x A100 + 4 x L4 to validate latency/tail behaviour and integration (no commitment, trial pricing + ramp credit applied if convert).
2) Transition (months 2–3): scale to 50% of reserved pool for testing and ingest validation.
3) Reserved live (month 4 onward): move to the full reserved pool as per SKU mix above; billing switches to committed monthly invoice with agreed discount tier.

Next steps / action items:
- Maya: confirm preferred workshop slot (we had Oct 12/13 proposed) — we can run an expedited workshop recording for stakeholders who missed it.
- Procurement: indicate which concession options are deal-breakers (early-termination cap, SLA language, or ramp credit).
- If you want, we can issue a PO-ready DocuSign link for the pilot PO; link: https://redwood.app/docs/docusign/ACM-PO-INIT

I’ll prepare a redlined procurement_terms_acme.docx with the concession selections once you tell us which of the above you want incorporated. Happy to hop on a 20–30m call to finalize.

Best,
